subject: Region-specific minimum logs: retention floor and erasure guarantees
messages:
From: Julie Fuentes <julie.fuentes@aurum.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurum AI Legal <legal@aurum.ai>
Date: 2027-12-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Data handling Qs re: DPA redlines

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the call earlier — Aurum is excited about using Redwood for production inference. Our legal team pushed back on the DPA draft and asked for a tighter commit on logs and geo residency. Two concrete asks:

1) We need a clause that prevents request/response logs being stored outside the EU for our tenant (we may accept a transient buffer for routing but it must not be persisted outside EU boundaries).
2) We asked for an explicit retention floor: minimal aggregated telemetry retained for at most 30 days; any request-level traces need a separate consent path and should be purgeable on demand with certification.

I've attached our redlines (Aurum_DPA_redlines_20271201.pdf). Can Redwood support a carveout that differentiates: (a) ephemeral routing/buffers, (b) short-term request logs (30d), (c) non-identifying aggregated telemetry (90d)?

Also, can you confirm whether backups/snapshots could be replicated for DR to the US, and if so, what legal & technical controls you can offer to keep Aurum's data from being read/accessed outside EU?

Appreciate any concrete wording you can propose.

Best,
Julie
VP Security, Aurum AI

Attachments: Aurum_DPA_redlines_20271201.pdf (pdf, 145KB)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Julie Fuentes <julie.fuentes@aurum.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-01T13:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Data handling Qs re: DPA redlines

Julie —

Thanks for the clear asks and the redlines. High level response first, then I included proposed contract language below that maps to your 3 buckets. Short answer: we can commit to EU-only persistent storage for customer data for the Aurum tenant, with a narrow set of exceptions for transient routing and explicit DR snapshots that we treat under strict legal & technical constraints.

Proposed mapping:
- Ephemeral routing/buffers: transient (<120s) memory/KV for inference; no persistence to disk outside region.
- Request-level logs: configurable by customer; default retention 30 days for request IDs and metadata; optional opt-in for longer for debugging with explicit export and purge APIs.
- Aggregated telemetry: non-identifying metrics can be retained up to 90 days by default.

Backing controls we can offer:
- Onshore (EU) primary storage for Aurum with geo-fencing: policy enforced at the infra/orchestrator level.
- If DR snapshots are enabled and travel to non-EU region, access is strictly limited to our SRE-run emergency playbook; access requires two-person approval and is logged to an audit trail available to Aurum.
- We will provide an erasure certification report within 72 hours after a purge request completes.

Draft contract snippet (high level):
"Redwood shall store Customer Data for the Aurum tenant within the European Economic Area (EEA). Temporary buffering and routing outside the EEA for not more than 120 seconds is permitted solely for the purpose of request routing and latency optimization and shall not be persisted. Persistent storage, backups, and snapshots shall remain within the EEA except where Disaster Recovery (DR) processes require replication outside the EEA. DR replication, if enabled, shall be subject to the access controls described in Appendix X (two-person access approval, restricted to named SREs, and customer-visible audit logs)."

I'll loop Legal for precise redline suggestions — Marissa, Rishi: can you review and suggest authoritative language for the DPA?

Naomi
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding Aurum's redlines and my outgoing note. Quick asks:

- Marissa: can you draft DPA language that 1) codifies EU-only persistent storage, 2) narrows "transient routing" to a max time window we can defend, and 3) specifies the audit/evidence we provide on erasure. Suggest we offer 72-hour certification for purge completion.
- Rishi: please confirm technical feasibility of the 120s buffer cap and whether our infra needs changes to ensure no disk spill to non-EU regions. If not feasible, propose an operable number.
- Monica: from an ops/contracting perspective, what admin process would we need to stand up two-person access and the emergency DR playbook for an enterprise tenant?

Notes from my call with Aurum: they are particularly sensitive to backups replicating outside EU for legal/regulatory reasons. They're willing to accept DR if we include strict access controls + an explicit workaround for certified deletion.

Thx — Naomi

Naomi — quick draft language below for the DPA (I've kept it terse to make it easy for the contract redline):

1) Regional persistent storage
"Redwood shall persist Customer Data associated with the Customer's account within data centers located in the European Economic Area (EEA). Persistent copies shall include object stores, database backups, and durable logs.

2) Transient buffering
"Transient buffering or caching that is necessary for request routing and inference execution may occur outside the EEA but shall be ephemeral in nature and not exceed {X} seconds; such data shall not be written to durable storage in non-EEA locations. Redwood will provide telemetry demonstrating no durable persistence in non-EEA regions upon Customer request."

3) Retention & on-demand erasure
"Customer may configure request-level retention; absent configuration, Redwood shall retain request-level logs no longer than 30 days. Aggregated, non-identifying telemetry may be retained for up to 90 days. Upon Customer request, Redwood shall initiate erasure of specified request-level data and provide a certification of completion within 72 hours of completion."

4) DR snapshots & limited exception
"If Disaster Recovery replication to non-EEA regions is enabled, Redwood shall restrict access to replicated copies to a named set of SREs and engineers and shall require two-person approval for any access to replicated Customer Data. All access shall be logged and the log shared with Customer on request."

Operational notes for Rishi & Monica:
- Rishi: I left the buffer duration as {X} — please replace with an operable value (suggestion: 120s or 300s if we need leeway). Also confirm whether we can assert 'no durable persistence' through config flags and infra guardrails.
- Monica: what artifact do we produce for the 72-hour certification (SRE-run job? signed pdf?) — we should propose a templated certification PDF plus audit logs export.

If everyone agrees, I'll return this to Naomi to send to Aurum with our proposed redline.

Marissa
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Naomi / team — thanks, that language is very helpful and closer to what we need. A few comments from legal after quick read:

- They want {X} replaced with a firm number. Aurum's preference is <= 60s for any cross-border transient buffer.
- Additional ask: explicit mention that telemetry must be "non-identifying" and include a sentence that Redwood will provide the aggregated telemetry schema so Aurum can verify no PII is present.
- Regarding DR: legal wants an explicit list of the job titles that can access DR replicas (not just "named SREs").

We can live with 120s if you cannot technically guarantee 60s, but please surface the operational controls you will use to prevent disk spill (e.g., node-level mounts, fs-level read-only flags, regional IAM scoping).

I'll await Rishi/Monica/Marissa's final wording.

Julie

Subject: Final: Redwood proposal — retention floors, buffer cap, and certification process

Julie / Aurum legal —

Thanks for the quick review and the specific asks; we discussed internally and below is our final proposal so you have an actionable redline to accept/reject. Key compromises: we can commit to a firm 120 second buffer cap for cross-border transient routing (60s was not operable across all infra patterns without risking timeouts), and we will publish the aggregated telemetry schema and provide signed erasure certifications.

Final proposed DPA redline text (ready to drop into your doc):

"1. Regional Persistent Storage: Redwood shall persist Customer Data associated with Customer's account within data centers located in the European Economic Area (EEA). Persistent copies include object stores, database backups, and durable logs.

2. Transient Buffering and Routing: Temporary buffering or caching necessary for request routing and inference execution may occur outside the EEA for a period not to exceed one hundred and twenty (120) seconds. Such transient data shall not be written to durable storage in non-EEA locations. Redwood will maintain infrastructure guardrails (regional IAM scoping, node-level mount policies, and monitoring alerts) to prevent unintended durable persistence and will provide telemetry on buffer usage upon Customer request.

3. Retention and Erasure: By default, request-level logs will be retained for a maximum of thirty (30) days. Aggregated, non-identifying telemetry will be retained for up to ninety (90) days. Redwood will publish the schema for aggregated telemetry and certify that no personally identifying information is included. Upon Customer request, Redwood will initiate erasure of specified request-level data and provide a signed erasure certification within seventy-two (72) hours of completion, together with audit logs documenting the operation.

4. Disaster Recovery (DR) Replication: If DR replication to non-EEA regions is enabled at Customer's direction, access to replicated copies shall be restricted to personnel holding the following job titles at Redwood: Site Reliability Engineer (SRE), Incident Response Lead, and Head of Cloud Operations. Access shall require two-person approval and be logged. Redwood will share access logs with Customer upon request and will only perform data access for the purpose of restoring Customer Data as part of DR procedures.

Operational commitments:
- Certification artifact: Redwood will provide a templated signed PDF erasure certification and a machine-readable audit export (CSV) for any purge request.
- Monitoring & proof: Redwood will expose a buffer-usage report for the Customer and periodic compliance attestations regarding regional persistence settings.

If Aurum is comfortable with this redline, we can accept your attached PDF with the edits, and Redwood's agreements team will prepare a clean DPA for signature. If you need the buffer cap tightened, we can propose a short trial where we aim for 60s and measure infra behavior, but we would need Aurum to acknowledge the trial risk to availability.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-erasure-playbook.pdf (operational playbook, 60 pages - attached)"
